shared.note: First successful end-to-end SFT -> RL/GRPO run of the CholecT50 triplet task in this benchmark. Managed GPUs via Thinking Machines Tinker; thin orchestration host (no local weights).
shared.eval: val split, n=300 frames, greedy decoding (temp 0); blended reward = 0.4*triplet_F1 + 0.6*mean(instrument, verb, target F1)

findings: Tinker runs RLVR/GRPO with a custom Python reward (the triplet-F1 Env) end to end with no platform gap — the whole point of this benchmark's CholecT50 leg.

SFT and RL use two non-interchangeable checkpoint kinds: save_state() -> weights/ (training, resumable) vs save_weights_for_sampler() -> sampler_weights/ (inference only). Eval of a training checkpoint requires converting to sampler_weights first.
Base model (Qwen3.5-4B, no fine-tuning) emits zero valid triplets (all F1 = 0.0), so SFT is the 'before'; RL then lifts every component (+17% triplet F1, +33% verb F1, +15% blended reward).
No per-job USD cost is surfaced by the SDK used; only token counts and wall time are available, so estimated_cost_usd is null.
Qwen3.5-4B (vision-language) LoRA fine-tuning + RL is supported on Tinker, the capability Together AI and Baseten could not self-serve for this task.
